notes:
The whole list (40 rows, the key, and the footer) is on n140.jpg, which is printed page 129. n139.jpg (p. 128) is the end of the report text, signed by More and Barrington on 19th May, 1885. n141.jpg (p. 130) has the List of Birds noticed. The list sits under the running head "IRISH COAST." and has no sub-headings, so coast is null throughout.

Columns: number; station and county; Spring. and Autumn reply marks (x / o / –); "Miles from shore." (– where none is given); "Names of Observers". The 'other' field gives these as "Spring …; Autumn …; Miles from shore …". There are no light characters in this list.

Checks: The printed numbering has no 9 (5.* and 8.* are used instead) and no 35. The 4 rows marked "No schedule sent." (4, 18, 31, 36) leave 36 stations, which matches "36 schedules sent out". Counting the marks gives 27 x in spring and 26 x in autumn, which matches the footer exactly. So every reply mark has been read correctly. In 'other' I've kept the footer's wording "replies received", but the key's x means "Schedule returned partly or wholly filled".

Where the image corrects the OCR:
- Row 1 is "Fastnet, Co.Cork" (the OCR garbled it).
- Row 7, Tuskar Rock, do. x x 7, "Richard Hamilton and Patrick D'Arcy", was badly garbled in the OCR.
- Row 27's observers are "John Redmond, J. Young and R. Lyons".
- Row 37 is "Tearaght", not "Learaght".
- Rows 36 and 40 have ½ mile, not "i" or "4".
- Row 32 is "Thomas Fortune".
- Row 13 is 3 miles, not 8.
- Rows 30 and 31 are 3 miles each, not 8.

Typesetting choices:
- Leader dots are left out of 'printed'.
- In the tightly set lines, 'printed' keeps the missing spaces as seen ("Co.Cork", "ArklowSth.Lt.-ship,Wicklow", "JohnRedmond"). The separate fields add normal word spaces ("Co. Cork", "Arklow Sth.", "John Redmond").
- Rows 5.* and 7 (two observers each) and row 27 (three) are set over two lines, joined by a brace in the observers column. I show the brace as "{" in 'printed'. It belongs to the names, not to the station, so marks is null for those rows.
- "No replies." is in italics (rows 2, 26, 34); "No schedule sent." is in roman type.
- "do." (ditto) stands for Wexford in rows 6 and 7 and for Wicklow in 8.*. Tuskar Rock (7) is "do." for the county only; it is not a light-ship.
- Number gives "5*" and "8*" as you asked; they are printed "5.*" and "8.*". The asterisk on 8.* is faintly or brokenly printed.
- Each light-vessel is printed with the type "Lt.-ship", not "L.V.".
- In 'name' I kept compass suffixes with the station ("Eagle Island, E.", "Slyne Head, N.", "Arran Island, S.").
- Row 3 is split as name "Old Head", place "Kinsale, Cork" (that is, Old Head of Kinsale).

Copied as printed, not corrected:
- Innishtrahull (usually Inishtrahull).
- Arranmore (usually Aranmore or Arranmore).
- Arran Island, N./S., Galway (the Aran Islands).
- Howth Baily (usually spelt Baily, so this is fine).
- Valentia.
- "Cunniam" (perhaps Cunningham or Cunnian; unverified).
- "Thomas Sweeny".

The same "Joseph Hill." is the observer at both Killybegs (22) and Oyster Island, N. Sligo (23). This may be one man, or a printer's repetition. Robt. W. Redmond (Blacksod Point) and John Redmond (Blackrock) are both Mayo stations. Keeper names keep their final full stop as printed, except the first name(s) in a joined pair or list.
